chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala, from Rifa'ah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who dies and did not perform the Hajj of Islam, and did not bequeath it, is it fulfilled on his behalf? He said: Yes.

key_terms.حَجَّةَ الْإِسْلَامِ: The first obligatory Hajj performed by a Muslim when able
key_terms.لَمْ يُوصِ بِهَا: Did not bequeath it (specifically allocate funds or instruction for it)
key_terms.يُقْضَى: Fulfilled / made up (as a debt or obligation)

ai.seo_question: Does a deceased person who did not perform Hajj in their lifetime have an outstanding obligation that is fulfilled on their behalf?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the obligatory Hajj (Hajj al-Islam) is a personal duty that persists after death if not performed, allowing heirs or others to fulfill it on the deceased's behalf even without a specific bequest. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly view that the spiritual debt of Hajj is transferable, ensuring the deceased's religious obligations are settled through the proxy performance of another Muslim.
